steps: Derive deadline versus timeout semantics, cancellation precedence, parent lifetime and nonextension of inherited budget. Distinguish stopping admission from acknowledgement and rollback.

Implement checked scope construction and cross-clock remaining-budget encoding, including zero budget, numeric horizon, depth exhaustion and stale parent-lifetime counterexamples without executing invalid access.
checks: Parent created at10 with budget10 expires20. A child at13 asking100 still expires20; at19 remaining is1 and at20 it is expired. Cancelling the parent makes the child CANCELLED. No borrowed storage becomes reclaimable solely because cancellation was requested.

units.title: Construct: Five overload policies and bounded pending producers
steps: Specify each policy in terms of observable loss, ordering, caller ownership and completion; distinguish application admission, transport buffering and receiver consumption.
Implement all five policies, closed draining and the real channel adapter, including exactly-once transfer and explicit retained pending state.
checks: Queue[1,2,3,4] plus DROP9 remains[1,2,3,4]; OVERWRITE9 becomes[2,3,4,9]; DEGRADE10 changes newest to10 and reports DEGRADED. BLOCK retains pending ownership. Expiry before a later retry terminates that offer without enqueuing it. A full imported channel leaves the local head in place.

Enumerate all policies at count0,1,3,4 with pending/closed/cancelled/expired states. Compare exact sequences with an independent list model. Drive a real MsgHub capacity1 to FULL and assert head preservation, then drain and retry. In the original malicious schedule, generate a burst beyond admission capacity and observe only bounded logical message loss/coalescing; no external traffic or host settings are involved.
reasoning: A fixed queue does not bound memory if arbitrary producers wait while retaining payloads. Overload policy changes the service contract and cannot be compared using throughput alone.
Specify each policy in terms of observable loss, ordering, caller ownership and completion; distinguish application admission, transport buffering and receiver consumption.
deliverables: Implement RZQueue/RZOffer with four copied unsigned messages and BLOCK, REJECT, DROP, OVERWRITE and DEGRADE policies exactly as CONTRACTS.md specifies. A blocked offer is a retained operation to retry, not a hidden sleeping thread. Degrade coalesces newest by max and reports reduced semantics. Implement rz_forward using your actual T73 nonblocking channel send and remove the head only on acceptance. Then add a bounded two-producer readiness adapter that registers before checking readiness, acknowledges cancellation and never creates an unbounded waiting-producer list.

units.title: Construct: Hashed timer-wheel collisions, cancellation and expiry work
steps: Derive bucket index, full due identity, list invariants and generation retirement. Prove why modulo bucket equality alone is insufficient across revolutions.
Implement bounded schedule/cancel/tick and a two-level cascade extension with no lost or duplicate expiries, explicit horizon, late tick and immediate timer policies.
checks: At now0 a delay5 timer maps to bucket1 but must not fire at tick1; it fires exactly at5. Cancelling generation1 then reusing that slot at generation2 makes the old ID STALE. Simultaneous due timers all appear in the returned mask, without invoking callbacks during linkage traversal.

Use an independent sorted map of absolute due times, not another wheel. Exhaust pairs of due1..16 and every cancellation point; verify back-links after each step. Add a delayed-clock jump that crosses three revolutions and either process all missed ticks or specify a bounded late-fire policy. Record the selected scheduler decision before measurement; historical paper VAX numbers are source observations only.
reasoning: The important wheel tradeoff is not merely replacing a comparison with modulo. Collisions, cancellation frequency, finite identity and concentrated expiries determine correctness and latency.
Derive bucket index, full due identity, list invariants and generation retirement. Prove why modulo bucket equality alone is insufficient across revolutions.
deliverables: Implement the four-bucket/four-slot wheel with delay1..16, absolute due ticks, intrusive index links and owner/generation identities. Tick advances one unit and returns every due slot as a bitmask; cancellation unlinks immediately. Extend to a two-level wheel that cascades coarse timers into fine buckets, preserving exact expiry and cancellation identity. Reopen the PR-T50-05 sealed scheduler decision and add this as a third measured alternative to its existing structures under the same timer contract.

Use an independent sorted map of absolute due times, not another wheel. Exhaust pairs of due1..16 and every cancellation point; verify back-links after each step. Add a delayed-clock jump that crosses three revolutions and either process all missed ticks or specify a bounded late-fire policy. Record the selected scheduler decision before measurement; historical paper VAX numbers are source observations only.

steps: Derive distinct health and capacity invariants, permit ownership, epoch identity and neutral-versus-backend-failure classification; explain why a failure window is not a concurrency bound.

checks: With limit1, a second simultaneous admission returns BUSY even while CLOSED. Two classified failures open. An older outstanding success releases capacity but leaves the newer OPEN state unchanged. At cooldown equality one probe may enter, a second is BUSY, and successful probe closes. Repeated completion is STALE.

Enumerate admit/fail/succeed/neutral sequences through each finite generation. Test old admission before two failures, then a late success after OPEN. reasoning: Health decisions summarize observations, while a bulkhead bounds admitted resource ownership. Conflating them allows an otherwise healthy slow backend to exhaust callers or an old completion to erase newer failure evidence.

checks: A new delta2 request applies once and queues its ID. Flush to channel0 allows msg_select to observe that exact ID. Filling the four pending slots rejects the next request before changing receiver.total. A full/cancelled imported channel retains pending notifications. Cancellation after an admitted effect cannot make its already-reserved notification disappear.

For the public anchor, fill/drain the real MsgHub, close/cancel it and compare pending IDs with receiver records. Mutation1 commits after notification capacity is exhausted; mutation2 discards an item without channel acceptance. For the full integration, enumerate each acquisition/failure prefix and replay randomized seeded event traces with an independent total/effect ledger. Retain exact compiler/link dependencies and actual measured traces. Do not record a simulated timer observation as hardware/network latency.
reasoning: Locally correct components can compose into lost committed notifications, duplicated effects, retry storms or premature cleanup. A service acceptance result needs a defined commit point and recovery policy, not a collection of successful unit tests.
